item.title: Brewers' Pat Murphy Disses Yankees During World Series Celebration
item.description: Milwaukee Brewers manager Pat Murphy The Milwaukee Brewers won their first World Series on Wednesday, and amid the celebration, manager Pat Murphy sent a diss to the New York Yankees while talking to Jake Bauers. Bauers, a free agent this offseason, came to give Murphy the ball from the final out of Game 5. The two embraced and Murphy shared some words with his breakout star. "You’re gonna be a rich (expletive)," Murphy said to Bauers in a video posted by Spectrum News 1 Wisconsin. "Just remember when you’re on that horse (expletive) Yankees team and you guys are all playing for yourselves, just remember this is the way we used to do it.” Bauers is bound to get paid after a breakout season at age 30. He led the Brewers in home runs and won World Series MVP. After bouncing around for years, struggling to establish himself in the big leagues, he considered retiring. Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? Check out our brand new baseball lifestyle brand! However, when his wife got pregnant, he decided to keep playing for the insurance benefits. What changed for him as a player? He says he stopped making it about himself and let the game come to him. He was more relaxed, focused on the now. It's no surprise he succeeded in Milwaukee, where every player has that mindset, seemingly. It's an uncommon mindset in baseball, and Murphy made it clear what he thinks of other teams like the Yankees, who can spend big and don't need to grind like the Brewers. The "built not bought" mantra will be very prevalent this offseason with whispers of a lockout. Big market teams like the Yankees have the luxury of spending on players who have great individual numbers. However, that does not always result in having the best team. Most of the Brewers team came up together, and it's no surprise they are so close. The guys who didn't grow up in the system, like Bauers, have all bought into the team mindset, and it's a huge factor in their success. item.title: The Valkyries told SF to call in sick. Meet the people who caught a flight.
item.description: Golden State Valkyries fans look on during the third quarter of Game 4 of the 2026 WNBA Finals against the Atlanta Dream at State Farm Arena on Oct. 24, 2026 in Atlanta. (Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) Head coach Natalie Nakase said Golden State Valkyries fans will ‘sacrifice' to watch Game 6, even though it'll be played entirely in the morning on Thursday in the Bay Area. But for hundreds of Valkyries fans at San Francisco International (SFO) Airport on Wednesday night, just watching from home wasn't good enough - they had to get to Atlanta, costs be damned. SFGATE went to SFO on Wednesday night and saw more than 50 fans in Valkyries gear boarding a nonstop flight on United to Atlanta around 9 p.m. on Wednesday. An hour later, over 100 more fans were decked out in violet, catching the nonstop flight on Frontier. Final destination: State Farm Arena for the chance to see the first-ever WNBA championship for the second-year team. "I think some of my family and friends think I'm crazy a little bit," Jess McPeak, a Valkyries season ticket holder who lives in the Mission, told SFGATE on Wednesday. "But the universe just gave me a path, almost magically." McPeak, who uses they/them pronouns, thought they were going to not be able to watch the game at all. They had a work meeting that directly conflicted with the 9:30 a.m. Pacific tip time . But on Tuesday, that meeting shifted and their day completely opened up. Pretty soon after, they were booking a trip to Atlanta, feeling like they "had to be there." Golden State Valkyries fan Jess McPeak of San Francisco poses outside of a San Francisco International Airport gate on Wednesday, Oct. 28, 2026 before flying to Atlanta for Game 6 of the WNBA Finals. (Alex Simon/SFGATE) They were not alone. Sirena Roberts, an Outer Sunset resident and Valkyries season ticket holder, has a remote job that has allowed her to attend every single WNBA Finals game of the series - yes, she flew out to Atlanta for Games 3 and 4 last week. "I just want to be a part of history, in case they clinch it," Roberts told SFGATE. As for funding the travel? "If I was going to blow all of my stored-up points for anything, it was going to be a last-minute Valkyries trip." At least half-a-dozen of the fans SFGATE spoke to said they funded their travel with stored up points. McPeak quipped they have "a s-t ton of miles I never use" on American, so they booked a flight to Atlanta through Miami on the way there and through Phoenix on the way back Thursday night. For many Valkyries fans , the reduced cost of flying allowed them to splurge for nicer seats inside State Farm Arena. Roberts said she paid $400 for seats near Golden State's tunnel on the first level. McPeak will also be on the lower level, saying they got tickets at the same price as their Valkyries season ticket has been for the Finals. item.title: 'Give every talent a chance' - Former Arsenal boss Arsene Wenger hails impact of innovative 8v8 FIFA U-15 World Cup featuring 189 nations in Azerbaijan
item.description: Arsene Wenger - 2026 FIFA U-15 World Cup & Festival - FIFA Former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger has praised the success of the inaugural FIFA U-15 World Cup and Festival in Baku after watching 189 member associations compete in a revamped eight-a-side format. Serving as FIFA's Chief of Global Football Development, the Frenchman believes the event bridges the gap between emerging and established nations. Global youth festival unites nations Wenger is delighted by how the week-long tournament has brought over 3,000 players, coaches and officials together in the Azerbaijani capital since kicking off on October 22. Approved by the FIFA Council in December 2025 for players born in 2011 or 2012, the competition uses smaller pitches and 20-minute halves. Nearly 1,000 matches are being staged across 20 simultaneous pitches at the purpose-built Hovsan Competition Complex. Modified format reduces gulf between countries Each delegation comprises 14 players and up to six staff members, competing in four or five round-robin group matches seeded by senior and youth rankings before entering six performance tiers for another four or five games. Speaking about the tournament's atmosphere and structure, Wenger said: "Well, the first thing that comes out is the image of happiness and excitement, because to see the whole world here together, and organise a tournament with basically 190 teams and do that all in one week, and [give them the chance] to live in the same place. The players look so happy, so committed, and to see the whole world like that, united, communicating, dancing, playing, is just what football should do always. "I would say it's working perfectly well. We wanted it to be a reduced number, not 11 against 11, because the difference between the countries would be too big. We wanted as well shorter games, you know, (so) that everybody can meet everybody. "In life, when you love a sport, you want to know how good you are. So, you have to play against everybody, so that the teams, the smaller countries, play against the bigger countries, and they can go home after, certainly full of dreams and of happy moments, but as well, they can know what they have to focus on to improve because they know where they stand. But it's as well, for us, for FIFA development, something that is very important." Smaller footballing nations gain belief Explaining how testing themselves against elite opposition helps emerging prospects realise their potential, the 77-year-old Frenchman added: "I don't believe that any country is entitled to have more success than [another], but number plays a part. But we have seen many smaller countries, you know, competing with the bigger countries so that is important that they meet, and like I told you, they can compete. item.description: Milwaukee Brewers players celebrate around pitcher Trevor Megill For the first time in their 58-year history, the Milwaukee Brewers are finally World Series champions. The Brewers were the best team in baseball wire-to-wire this year, leading MLB and setting a franchise record with a 103-59 record during the regular season. item.title: Cody Gakpo On Chelsea Win and Return of Anfield’s Energy
item.description: At this point a year ago, hope was fading and the mood was souring around Liverpool. A side expected to at least mount something resembling a defence of their title from the season before was struggling both to deliver strong performances and good results. Worse than that, perhaps, they were sinking into an increasingly passive shell. For a time, the home crowds tried to do their part. Yet as it became clear the team were getting stuck ever deeper in their reactive rut, either unable due to circumstances or unwilling due to tactics to play a more passionate and proactive game, even that slipped away. If the team wasn’t going to play a passionate brand of football—for whatever reason—then Anfield was always going to struggle to find their own passion across the length and breadth of the season. Two months into Andoni Iraola’s tenure as manager, it’s clear the passion is back. On both sides. “Everybody in the stands knows when we have a little bit of momentum or a good moment then they get behind us with everything they’ve got,” forward Cody Gakpo said following Wednesday’s penalty shootout victory over Chelsea in the League Cup. “I have to say, it always gives us energy nobody thought they had. It’s very helpful and obviously we are very appreciative of that and we always try to give back. So here we obviously had a little advantage with the crowd and being at home, so that was nice. I think in the end it’s a good win.” Last season, the players and the fans almost seemed to get stuck in a negative feedback loop. The players were more passive and played a more reactive game and the energy in the stands dropped and individual errors on the pitch were punished and nobody on either side was able to find the wherewithal to react and the energy both on and off the pitch dropped further. It’s not what anyone would have wanted. There were good reasons to explain why it might have started. But once stuck in it, it became self-reinforcing and nobody involved seemed to know how to do anything but dig the hole deeper. On the evidence of the early season and last night against Chelsea, that ability for the fans to push the players at times as well as for the players to ask for help—and receive it—with a well-timed moment of passion and effort is back. And with it, the Reds are into the quarter-finals of the League Cup. “The further you go in the tournament the closer it gets to silverware and it’s a competition wthathich goes fast with the final in February or March,” Gakpo added. “So it can be quick silverware for the team and it can also give you a boost for the end of the season as well.”

item.title: Andy Reid’s comments on Justin Tucker signing shows hollowness of NFL coachspeak
item.description: Credit: Kansas City Chiefs, Denny Medley-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect Kansas City Chiefs head coach Andy Reid has steered his team through off-field controversy and personal tragedy countless times in his storied NFL career. Reid’s steadiness has served him well. He has the fourth-most wins among head coaches in NFL history, including three Super Bowls, and he will walk into the Pro Football Hall of Fame. Reid’s players love him , and his peers revere him, so his words carry significant weight. Reid has also been remarkably consistent in his press-conference approach. He’s famously a man of few words, save for an iconic line about the Grim Reaper or jokes about cheeseburgers . In most cases, fans find it endearing, even if reporters find it frustrating. But in consequential moments that demand more, like this week, Reid’s overreliance on coachspeak falls flat. On Wednesday, the Chiefs signed former Baltimore Ravens All-Pro kicker Justin Tucker to their practice squad. Tucker, 36, served a 10-game suspension last season after 16 women came forward and alleged Tucker engaged in sexual misconduct during massage sessions across Baltimore. The Ravens released Tucker in May 2025, and he remained unsigned until now. Tucker has denied all allegations . Upon the Chiefs giving Tucker new NFL life, one of Tucker’s alleged victims told the Baltimore Banner that it was “sickening.” Meanwhile, Andy Reid opened his Wednesday press conference with mundane niceties and updates before offering his signature phrase, “With that, time’s yours.” Predictably, reporters had plenty of Tucker questions, and Reid responded with unsettling nonchalance when Mac Morey asked what message signing Tucker sends to women in the Chiefs’ fan base. “Yeah, so, he’s done his suspension, you know. Took care of that business there,” Reid said. “I’ll leave it at that for you.” When asked about the involvement of ownership in signing Tucker, Reid offered, “Yeah, listen, we try to do our homework the best way we possibly can. Talk to a lot of people and make sure things are OK.” The line of questioning pivoted to Tucker’s on-field decline and Chiefs kicker Harrison Butker’s league-worst performance dating back to last year. Later, Reid was asked to explain the thought process behind his “long history of giving players second chances.” Reid said, “I try to do homework on it and see exactly what’s taken place since. item.title: Takeaways From Knicks’ 19-Point Comeback Win Versus Bulls
item.description: Oct 28, 2026; Chicago, Illinois, USA; New York Knicks guard Jalen Brunson (11) points after scoring during the second half against the Chicago Bulls at United Center. Mandatory Credit: Matt Marton-Imagn Images | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Benjamin Yu, Editor After the New York Knicks ended their winless start on Tuesday night in a 111-97 win over the Detroit Pistons, the defending champions got their second win of the season on Wednesday night. The Knicks overcame a 19-point third-quarter deficit to beat the Chicago Bulls 133-127 at the United Center. Here are some takeaways from Wednesday night’s win. Jalen Brunson Is Back Jalen Brunson finally looked like himself again on Wednesday night after a lackluster start to the season. In his 35 minutes, the Knicks’ captain scored a season-high 38 points on 13-25 shooting, including 6-10 from beyond the arc, along with seven assists. In vintage Brunson fashion, he made most of his impact in the fourth quarter, scoring 14 in the final period of the game. It was far and away the best performance Brunson has had this season. A major factor in the Knicks’ slow start over the first week of the season was a slew of lackluster outings from the 2026 NBA Finals MVP. While he did have surgery on his left wrist in July, he was still back for training camp and the preseason, so he had more than enough time to get his sea legs. Brunson finally seemed to have done so and will be expected to keep the level he displayed on Wednesday night throughout the rest of the season. The Bench Is Still Strong Along with Brunson’s second-half heroics, a major key to the Knicks’ comeback win was the performance of their bench. This was incredibly important on Wednesday as it was another night where Mikal Bridges failed to make a real impact on the game. The substitutes that made the most impact were Jordan Clarkson , Landry Shamet , and Tyler Kolek . After not playing at all on Tuesday night, Clarkson scored 18 points in his 17 minutes, with 12 coming in the fourth quarter. Clarkson also had two steals on the defensive end of the floor. Shamet played most of the minutes that Bridges would normally have, and hit four three-pointers amid his 14 points and five assists. Kolek has seen a massive minutes increase over the last three games with Jose Alvarado out, and he really proved his worth on Wednesday. He went 3-4 from beyond the arc and dished out a team-high nine assists. The bench is a pivotal part of how this Knicks team will get through the grind of the regular season. On Wednesday night, New York’s bench also reminded NBA fans of their ability to make up for, or even exceed, a starter’s production if one was out, or, in the case of Wednesday, not playing nearly well enough. item.description: AUBURN, ALABAMA - OCTOBER 24: Jordan Seaton #77 and Sam Leavitt #10 of the LSU Tigers in action against the Auburn Tigers at Jordan-Hare Stadium on October 24, 2026 in Auburn, Alabama. Let’s take a minute to acknowledge several impact players who have shown up and carried this team since Week 1. Offensive Lineman of the Midseason: Jordan Seaton Seaton will be, and should be, the number one OT selected in the draft this spring, and deservedly so. This LSU offense has had its moments of feeling stuck in the mud, but that was not a result of Seaton’s play. item.title: ‘Still shooting that thang’ – Mike Brown’s hilarious reaction to Karl-Anthony Towns’ wrist injury
item.description: Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images Karl-Anthony Towns seemingly injured his wrist against the Chicago Bulls, but returned later in the game to deliver a strong performance. The Knicks are finally back to winning ways, earning their second win of the season against the Chicago Bulls on the road. During the game, Karl-Anthony Towns had to go back to the locker room after injuring his wrist in the first quarter after a collision with Bulls star Noa Essengue. Mike Brown seemingly unfazed by Karl-Anthony Towns’ wrist injury During his post-game press conference following the New York Knicks’ win over the Chicago Bulls, Mike Brown responded to a question about the nature of Karl-Anthony Towns’ wrist injury. In his typically sarcastic tone, Brown joked that Towns was still able to make shots from deep, and the wrist didn’t seem to bother him. Brown said: “He was still shooting that thang from 30 feet! So the wrist looked okay to me.” Towns would end up leaving the game after a collision with Noa Essengue during the first quarter. Some fans were worried that he wouldn’t return to the game. However, Towns decided to tough it out, taping his wrists and returning to the game to help the Knicks pull off a much-needed win. Towns ended the game with a double-double, putting up 19 points, 13 rebounds, five assists, and a steal, while shooting 50% from both the field and from beyond the arc. Losing Towns to a long-term injury would have only compounded the poor start the Knicks have made this season, especially considering the circumstances. The Knicks started the season 0-3, becoming the first NBA Champions to lose their first three games since the 2011 Dallas Mavericks. On top of that, given the stalemate Towns and the Knicks are in over a new contract, an extended absence from the team would have caused trade rumours to intensify. item.title: Sophie Cunningham makes ’20 seconds’ anthem plea as WNBA Finals reach Game 6
item.description: Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham told Theo Von that WNBA teams leaving the court for the national anthem is nothing new this season, and the pending free agent tied her stance to military families and a call for more unity among players. “This has been happening throughout the whole season,” Cunningham said on This Past Weekend. “People are just kind of getting mad about it now.” She added, “I take a lot of pride in where I come from, and I’m proud to be an American citizen .” MORE: Sophie Cunningham reveals FBI is watching 20 stalkers as alleged stalker stays jailed What does Cunningham do during the national anthem? Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham (8) in the first half against the Seattle Storm | Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images The 30-year-old guard pointed to relatives who wore the uniform. “We have family members who have served, and they’re over there doing things that are unimaginable for us to be out here living our dreams,” she said. “So anytime that I can shout out our veterans and the people who are currently fighting for us, I’m going to show that support,” Cunningham said. “That doesn’t mean that’s where everyone stands.” She also boiled the moment down to a simple request. “Okay, this isn’t about me. I need 20 seconds of your best behavior,” she said. Cunningham has seen the walkouts from the floor. When Indiana visited Atlanta on Aug. 18, Dream players stayed off the court for the anthem while the Fever lined up and Cunningham held her hand over her heart, prompting Alabama Sen. Tommy Tuberville to post, “Sophie Cunningham is a true PATRIOT .” WNBA Finals anthem walkouts Singer Alanis Morissette sings the national anthem before game two of the 2026 WNBA Finals featuring the Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries at Chase Center. | David Gonzales-Imagn Images The Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries left the court before the anthem at Game 1 of the Finals on Oct. 17 at Chase Center and returned about two minutes later, a routine both teams kept through the series. The 2026 WNBA rulebook calls for players, coaches and trainers to “ stand and line up along the sidelines or foul line” during the anthem. Valkyries coach Natalie Nakase said, “We’re two years in. That’s been part of our pregame .” Trump urged fans to tune out at an Iowa rally. “The NFL did that for a while, and they stopped because people stopped watching the games,” Trump said. “So I think you should do the same thing with women’s basketball.” Golden State leads the series 3-2 entering Game 6, Valkyries at Dream, Thursday at 12:30 p.m. ET in Atlanta. item.description: UNCASVILLE, CONNECTICUT - OCTOBER 12: Uche Izoje #44 of the Syracuse Orange plays against the Connecticut Huskies during the second half of an NCAA women's exhibition basketball game at Mohegan Sun Arena on October 12, 2026 in Uncasville, Connecticut. (Photo by Joe Buglewicz/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Syracuse Orange women’s basketball team will be searching for a first in coach Felisha Legette-Jack’s tenure: back-to-back NCAA Tournament appearances. With the start of the year almost here, it appears the Orange will at least be in the conversation. Syracuse will enter the 2026-27 season projected as an 11-seed for the 2027 NCAA Tournament, according to ESPN’s latest bracketology update from Charlie Creme, which was released Tuesday. Syracuse is one of 10 ACC teams projected to make the 2027 field, which will now include 76 teams instead of 68. The rest of the list includes Duke (one-seed), Louisville (two-seed), North Carolina (three-seed), Notre Dame (four-seed), NC State (seven-seed), Virginia Tech (eight-seed), Clemson (eight-seed), Virginia (10-seed), and California (12-seed). Here’s the full breakdown of the ACC squads: Duke: one-seed Louisville: two-seed North Carolina: three-seed Notre Dame: four-seed NC State: seven-seed Virginia Tech: eight-seed Clemson: eight-seed Virginia: 10-seed Syracuse: 11-seed California: 12-seed The ACC is in a three-way tie with the SEC and Big 12 for most projected bids, per Creme. The Big Ten leads all conferences with 13. Nine ACC teams, including Syracuse, make the 2026 NCAA Tournament. The Orange will play nine of their 18-game conference schedule against opponents projected to make the tournament, according to this latest bracketology. Syracuse’s full 2026-27 schedule includes two other projected tournament teams: Oklahoma (six-seed) at home and Southern (16-seed) in Puerto Rico. Syracuse has reached the NCAA Tournament twice in four years (2024 and 2026) during Legette-Jack’s tenure with the Orange. Syracuse last earned consecutive trips to the Big Dance in 2018 and 2019. The Orange will begin their quest to reach the postseason on Tuesday at home against Sacred Heart.

item.title: ‘My bad’ – Tom Brady sends out apology to 49ers fans after what he said about them
item.description: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers lost their unbeaten title at the weekend following their shock loss to the Atlanta Falcons. Kyle Shanahan’s team are now set to enjoy their Bye Week after what has been a seriously impressive start to the season. Their 6-1 record has the Niners sitting top of the NFC West but the Minnesota Vikings have taken their one seed in the conference. Following victories against the Los Angeles Rams and the Seattle Seahawks, it would not have been unfair for a lot of people to overlook the Falcons heading into last weekend’s game. However, Tom Brady has issued an apology to the Niners fans after feeling as if he had jinxed their team going into Sunday’s loss. Tom Brady apologises for cursing the San Francisco 49ers For weeks, the Niners have sat top of Brady’s weekly power rankings as they remained unbeaten through the opening six weeks of the season. Heading into the game, Brady was convinced the Niners would make it seven wins from seven which now has him apologising to the Niners fans. “Down go the Niners, not very far, and I may have jinxed this last one last week when I said they cruise into their bye at a perfect 7-0. One of my first announcer jinxes, my bad, guys. They get a well-timed bye this week as the injuries continue to pile up for the Niners, but as I’ve said before, I think Kyle Shanahan and John Lynch have built a team capable of withstanding it,” said Brady in his Week Seven rankings. “Brock [Purdy] was not great in Atlanta, simple as that, and I know he’ll be in the film room and ready to go next time out.” There had been some close calls for the Niners in their opening six victories with the win in Seattle seeing both teams doing their best to lose the game on offense. While the Niners almost blew it against the Washington Commanders in the week following. A long season still lies ahead and it is now clear that there are ways to beat the Niners. Shanahan will be hoping the Bye Week can help bring back some of his injured players as they look to avoid a similar situation to last year when they entered the postseason with a depleted roster. item.title: Arizona Fall League Check-In
item.description: The Twins and all of their minor league affiliates have been done playing for a month now, but the Arizona Fall League is in full swing, and a handful of Twins minor leaguers are still playing. For those who don’t know much about the AFL, it is typically not a place where you see top 100 prospects dueling on a nightly basis. The Twins send 8 players each season to team up with minor leaguers from 4 other MLB organizations, mostly consisting of players who dealt with injuries during the summer and didn’t play as many games as the team hoped for. The pitching side has been a struggle as left-handers Cesar Lares and Ross Dunn have struggled to get outs, and Brian Zeldin has had limited opportunities, throwing just 2.1 innings across 5 appearances. Lares and Dunn are continuing to recover from major arm injuries that cost them the entire 2025 season along with a good portion of the 2026 season. Lefty reliever Cleiber Maldonado has been a bright spot in a small sample size. After missing the entire 2025 season while recovering from elbow surgery, Maldonado made his return in July. He posted a 12.60 ERA, walking 16 batters in 15 innings but showed off impressive stuff, striking out 23 and running impressive whiff rates. In 4 AFL appearances, he has allowed 2 earned runs in 4.1 innings while striking out 7 and walking 3. Maldonado was playing well as a 20-year-old southpaw in Single-A before the elbow injury, and he is showing good signs this fall as the Twins hope for a breakout in 2027. It was an uninspiring 2026 season for my No. 27 Twins prospect Kyle DeBarge . He played 120 games at Double-A, showing off excellent middle infield defense along with valuable speed on the bases, but the bat just never got there… until now, because DeBarge has been one of the hottest hitters in Arizona this fall, batting .367 with a 1.071 OPS in 14 games so far. He is still striking out too much for a smaller guy with limited raw power, but the swing decisions and walk rates have continued to improve throughout the season, and he is developing a nice feel for pulling fly balls. There is a limited ceiling on this profile, but DeBarge could carve out a major league bench role with his speed and defense. This one goes out of the park! item.title: Inter Still Dipping Their Toes in the Wing-Back Market
item.description: Inter Still Dipping Their Toes in the Wing-Back Market Inter signed Djed Spence and are close to coming to terms with Carlos Augusto , but that hasn’t stopped them from keeping tabs on a few players in such a role for the future, in particular Romano Floriani Mussolini and Pedrinho, Tuttomercatoweb reports. The former netted his maiden goal against Sassuolo. He has been playing a lot since Adam Marusic got hurt for the high-flying Lazio. He’s under contract only until 2028 with a very low salary, €130k. The Biancocelesti have started discussing an extension and a pay bump to €500k annually, with gradual increases. He spent previous seasons on loan at Pescara, Juve Stabia and Cremonese. Inter could target Floriani Mussolini in January or next June if they offload Luis Henrique . They’d need to find the right offer, as their outcast wasn’t cheap. The Brazilian has been relegated to a minuscule role since Andy Diouf took over the position. Plus, Spence will play increasingly more after dealing with physical problems. The Nerazzurri scouted Pedrinho from up close in the last UEFA Champions League fixture. He’s more versatile and offensive-minded, but they have been searching for that kind of player for a while. He has a €25M price tag and has tallied 16 goals and 20 assists in 97 since joining from Atletico Mineiro in 2024. Our Take on Inter, Floriani Mussolini, and Pedrinho Henrique has been for sale for multiple windows, and the longer it takes, the more his valuation will decrease. They like to invest in Italian players and can be very convincing economically, but it’d be stunning if Lazio sold their starlet anytime soon.

item.title: Lions QB Jared Goff is finally getting the respect he deserves
item.description: DETROIT,MICHIGAN-OCTOBER 25: Quarterback Jared Goff #16 of the Detroit Lions walks off the field after an NFL football game between the Green Bay Packers and the Detroit Lions in Detroit, Michigan USA, on Sunday, October 25, 2026 (Photo by Jorge Lemus/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images Detroit Lions quarterback Jared Goff has almost never been in the top-five quarterback conversation for his entire career. He got some accolades early during his time with the Los Angeles Rams, but ever since he was traded to the Detroit Lions for what the Rams deemed an upgrade in Matthew Stafford, Goff has been commonly viewed as a second, third or even fourth-tier quarterback. However, his work in rebuilding the Detroit Lions into a contender over the past six years has started to turn some doubters into believers. Some still pushed back, giving people like former Lions offensive coordinator Ben Johnson most of the credit. But even NFL executives and coaches have started to consider Goff a top-10 quarterback in recent years. Still, he’s rarely mentioned among the likes of Patrick Mahomes, Lamar Jackson, Josh Allen, Joe Burrow, and Stafford. But there’s something in the air this week. Goff currently leads the NFL with a 112.5 passer rating. He’s also first in passing yards per game, and adjusted yards gained per attempt. And perhaps most distinguishingly, Goff is the only quarterback with over 120 passing attempts this year who has yet to throw an interception. His +14 touchdown-to-interception ratio is two ahead of the next-closest quarterback (Burrow: 15 TDs, 3 INTs). And so after dismantling an impressive Green Bay Packers defense last week, Goff is getting a ton of national attention that I can’t ever recall seeing in year’s past. Over on CBS Sports, Garrett Podell put Goff as the No. 1 quarterback in his weekly QB power rankings . “His 14 touchdowns without an interception are also tied for the most in NFL history in that span, along with Russell Wilson in the 2019 season,” Podell wrote. “Fresh off winning his duel with Jordan Love and the Green Bay Packers at the last second, Goff also ranks second in expected points added (EPA) per dropback (0.29), just one one-hundredth behind Josh Allen (0.30). However, Goff has been the much better passer this season, which gets him the nod for the top spot entering Week 8.” Former NFL offensive lineman Mark Schlereth made an impassioned argument that Goff is unequivocally a top-five quarterback in this league on the OG Football Show: “We get so enamored with guys’ ability to scramble and make plays and be off-schedule and scramble around and make a big throw down the middle. Jared Goff processes and he delivers. He is so deadly accurate,” Schlereth said. item.title: Three keys to a Gopher win and how to watch
item.description: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - OCTOBER 03: Minnesota Golden Gophers defensive lineman TJ Bush Jr. (3) celebrates pressuring Michigan Wolverines quarterback Bryce Underwood (19) which lead to an interception during the second half to the college football game between the Michigan Wolverines and the Minnesota Golden Gophers on October 3rd, 2026, at Huntington Bank Stadium in Minneapolis, MN. (Photo by Bailey Hillesheim/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Next up for the Gophers is another trip to the state of Indiana to face the defending national champions. If one had been in a coma or a cave for the last 18 months, one would think we are heading to South Bend. But no, it’s Bloomington. How to Watch TV: CBS Time: 2:30 Stream: CBSSports Neither of these offenses have been lighting the Big Ten on fire lately. Minnesota has scored just 49 points in their last three games and Indiana has scored just 48. Is this going to be another rock fight? Will it come down to special teams and turnovers? Can Minnesota steal a massive win in Bloomington? KEYS TO A GOPHER WIN Points off turnovers – Considering how much the Gopher offense has struggled for most of the season, I don’t anticipate scoring much (if at all) against this Hoosier defense. They are very good. But if we can find a way to score off a turnover or on special teams…this game may be within reach. Cover their receivers – While Josh Hoover isn’t nearly the same as having Fernando Mendoza, the Hoosiers still have elite receivers in Charlie Becker and Nick Marsh. Becker is a certain first-round pick next spring, while Marsh will hear his name on day 2, at the latest. This will be the biggest challenge for our secondary. Paging Anthony Smith – 15 tackles and 1.5 sacks through seven games is not the kind of production we need from Smith. He needs a breakout game and this would be the perfect time for it. OPPOSING PLAYERS TO WATCH #80 WR – Charlie Becker – Is he the best receiver in the Big Ten? No, but he’s still likely a top-10 pick in the draft and any other year he would be the best receiver in the Big Ten. #12 DL – Tobi Osunsanmi – Osunsanmi leads the Big Ten with nine sacks and he absolutely could wreck the Gopher offense on his own. PREDICTION It has been Indiana’s MO to start slow and pull out the win late. Nebraska was up 11 in the fourth quarter, Ohio State was up 19-7 and only held on because Nick Marsh casually stepped out of bounds, and their win over Michigan was 6-6 in regulation before the Hoosiers scored in OT to win. They are finding ways to win later in games and I think Saturday afternoon will be similar. While the offense takes their time to get going, the defense is elite. I do not love this matchup of the Gopher offense up against this Hoosier D and I expect to see a lot of Tom Weston and if we can manage to find short fields, maybe some Luke Drzewiecki. We will hang around, but fall short. Minnesota – 9 Indiana – 17

The key to Cam Young ‘s success throughout his career to date has been his incredible driving. He was ranked 15th in driving distance on the PGA Tour in 2026, 13th in strokes gained off the tee and 13th in total driving. So, it goes without saying that any tips he has to offer should be grasped with both hands by amateur golfers who are looking to improve off the tee. Cam Young’s advice for amateur golfers who want to hit the high draw Young recently explained how he goes about ripping a high draw off the tee with his driver during an instructional video on YouTube. “ When I go to hit a draw, I don’t like it to be from here (from the inside) and kind of throwing it with my arms, “ Young explained. “ So I feel like I try to get it kind of, you know, out in front of me and turning over that way as opposed to from underneath. “ When I start launching them really high and loopy, that’s when I know I’m kind of not my favourite spot. “ I always kind of work to get it up in the front of my stance, and make sure that my forearms get underneath a little bit that way. “ And then in the swing, for me, it’s kind of making sure that I don’t get too inside on the takeaway, because from there, I feel like if the club is out in front of me here, I can make sure that it’s going the right direction. Christos Tzolis made a very fine start to life at Arsenal after joining the Gunners from Club Brugge in the summer , and he has been one of the top performers in their team so far. item.title: If you could change the outcome of one Phillies game, which would it be?
item.description: PHILADELPHIA, PA - OCTOBER 24: Bryce Harper #3 of the Philadelphia Phillies reacts to flying out in the seventh inning during Game 7 of the NLCS between the Arizona Diamondbacks and the Philadelphia Phillies at Citizens Bank Park on Tuesday, October 24, 2023 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Rob Tringali/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images One of the first lessons you learn as a fan of sports is that you can’t win em’ all. It’s become a hackneyed phrase, but it is an unalienable truth one must accept if you’re going to emotionally invest yourself in a team, especially in a sport like baseball where even the best teams still lose roughly 60 games a year. That doesn’t mean that certain losses don’t sting, and some may even leave emotional scarring that could take years to heal if ever. But what if you could undo the result of one of those games that still haunt you to this day. There are of course numerous examples from Phillies history, with perhaps the most famous being Game 6 of the 1993 World Series. Who knows what would have happened if Mitch Williams successfully locked down the save and forced a decisive Game 7 over the Blue Jays? Maybe the Phillies would have ended their Cinderella season with a ring. At the very least, an entire generation of Phillies fans would have been spared trauma. There are some more recent examples too. The 2023 NLCS will go down in infamy in Philadelphia, but what if the Phillies were able to close it out in Game 6 or even in Game 7 to win their second straight NL pennant? It’s not hard to see them possibly going on to win their elusive third championship in their franchise history and making it easier to look back on this era fondly. So, if you could change the outcome of one Phillies fame, which would it be? Would you undo Joe Carter? What about making it so that you never have to think about Kevin Ginkel again? Or maybe there’s one particular regular season loss that has lived in your head for your own personal reason.

item.title: The Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders Are Unionizing, but in 1995, One Now-Defunct NFL Cheer Squad Became the First to Do So
item.description: The Buffalo Jills cheerleaders performed at the Super Bowl in 1993 in Pasadena, Calif. Credit: Gin Ellis/Getty NEED TO KNOW While the Dallas Cowboys recently voluntarily recognized the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders Association as the dancers’ collective bargaining organization, the squad is not the first NFL cheer team to unionize The Buffalo Jills, the former cheer squad for the Buffalo Bills, unionized in 1995 The Jills disbanded in 2022 after the settlement of a $7.5 million lawsuit in which former members of the squad alleged that they had not been properly compensated for their hours worked Last week, the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders , one of the most recognizable cheer teams in the National Football League, voted to unionize. After a years-long, public fight for fair pay, the Cowboys voluntarily recognized the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders Association as the team’s collective bargaining organization, a joint statement from the team and the DCAA, published by ESPN , said. “The Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders are an esteemed part of the Cowboys organization, deeply respected for the talent and dedication they exhibit. They remain one of the most sought-after opportunities for talented dancers worldwide,” the release read. The Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders perform before a game on Oct. 8, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. Credit: Ron Jenkins/Getty The decision to unionize comes after the dancers’ struggles in seeking fair pay have made headlines over the last few years. With the popularity of the Netflix show America’s Sweethearts : Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders, public scrutiny intensified once more over the pay that the DCC — many of whom also work full-time day jobs to pay bills and cover expenses — receive for their work. Following the second season of the show, which touched on some of the contract negotiations between the Dallas Cowboys organization and the cheerleaders themselves, the dancers were able to secure a pay raise from $15 per hour during the 2024 season to $75. However, while the DCC remains one of the most relevant and recognizable cheerleading organizations in the NFL and their fight for better pay and working conditions has been widely followed, they are not the first squad to unionize. Only one other team has attempted to do so — the Buffalo Jills in 1995, then the official cheerleading squad of the Buffalo Bills. The Buffalo Jills were founded in 1967 by Jo Ann Gaulin, and remained active until 2022. Members of the Buffalo Jills cheer before a game on Jan. 26, 1992 in Minneapolis, Minn. Credit: Gin Ellis/Getty In 1995, the squad members became the first NFL cheerleading squad to unionize under the National Labor Relations Board, according to the Buffalo Jills Alumni website . item.description: Stipe Miocic has made his prediction for Ciryl Gane vs Josh Hokit, as the pair prepare to vie over the heavyweight legend’s old title . Miocic first held the UFC heavyweight belt from 2016 to 2018, winning a record-breaking three title defences, before reigning again from 2019 until 2021. After his second reign was ended by Francis Ngannou, the American fought just once more, losing to then-champion Jon Jones via TKO in 2024 . Miocic retired in the cage after the fight. That bout was just one chapter in a chaotic spell for the UFC’s heavyweight division; Jones vacated the title in summer 2025 after turning down $30m to face interim champion Tom Aspinall , who was subsequently elevated to undisputed champion. However, Aspinall’s first defence of the regular belt ended as a first-round no-contest, when he was poked in the eyes numerous times by Gane. Stipe Miocic (left) during his retirement fight against Jon Jones in 2024 (Getty) Britain’s Aspinall vacated the title this September, 11 months after facing Gane, due to ongoing complications from the eye injury he sustained against the Frenchman. Gane was thus elevated to undisputed champion, having won the interim belt by stopping Alex Pereira at the White House in June. Gane’s first defence of the undisputed title will come against Hokit on 14 November , when he fights the controversial American in the main event of UFC 334 – at Madison Square Garden, where Miocic retired.
